root_idea.development: The supplied lexical evidence centers on duration that continues without interruption; a related adjectival derivative extends this idea to what has neither beginning nor end.

qac_form_accounting.reason: The Quran-attested noun is presented under the normalized citation form سَرْمَد.

senses.usage_conditions: In the Quran, it is applied to night or day when conceived as continuing without interruption. The same perpetuity sense can also be used predicatively with the meaning “ever” or “forever.”

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having neither beginning nor end; eternal.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Adjectival derivative describing something without a beginning or an end.

lane_unit_coverage.note: Continuance or incessant continuance of time is covered by the Quranic duration sense.
Endless continuation applied to night and day is explicitly Quran-attested.
The predicative “ever/forever” expression adds no distinct semantic branch.
The adjectival meaning of having neither beginning nor end is separately represented.

cautions: No Maqāyīs evidence was supplied; the root orientation is therefore based on the supplied direct lexical evidence.
